report.source_text: The patient was treated initially with intravenous dexamethasone 4 mg three times daily for 3 days, followed by oral prednisone (30 mg/day) in conjunction with dapsone at increasing doses: 50 mg/day during the first week; 75 mg/day during the second week; and 100 mg/day thereafter. Hormonal therapy with letrozole 2.5 mg/day was also started. A nasogastric feeding tube was initially necessary, but a rapid clinical improvement in the pharynx and larynx allowed the patient to resume oral intake.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid (MMP) with diffuse oral, ocular, nasal, cutaneous, pharyngeal and laryngeal involvement
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of diffuse oral burning, disabling pharyngodynia, weight loss, and asthenia, accompanied by respiratory symptoms (cough when lying down, hoarseness, dyspnoea), bilateral ocular irritation, and nail inflammation. She had a remote history of treated breast and endometrial carcinoma without recurrence. Initial empiric treatments with topical/systemic antifungal, antibiotic, and antiviral therapies failed. Two prior oral biopsies demonstrated fibrin deposits with leucocytes but no malignant cells. Diagnostic confirmation was achieved via direct immunofluorescence revealing linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermo-epidermal junction, with negative indirect immunofluorescence. Comprehensive evaluation documented extensive mucosal involvement: nasal endoscopy revealed crusts on the right middle turbinate/nasopharynx and diffuse whitish pseudomembrane-covered erosions of the supraglottic area and posterior hypopharyngeal wall; clinical examination confirmed bilateral conjunctival inflammation and blister-type skin lesions on the arms and legs. Treatment with intravenous dexamethasone followed by oral prednisone and dapsone (titrated to 100 mg/day) resulted in rapid clinical improvement, allowing discontinuation of nasogastric feeding and resumption of oral intake.
